I'll look through the notes folder first so the naming and index match what's already there.The minutes use mixed names and one file is dated the day the meeting was postponed. I'll rename them to `YYYY-MM-DD.md` by the day each meeting was held, and add an index.The minutes in `notes/` now share one name pattern, and `notes/index.md` lists them in date order.

Every file is `YYYY-MM-DD.md`, using the day the meeting was held:

| Old name | New name |
| --- | --- |
| `aug11.md` | `2026-08-11.md` |
| `minutes 25 aug.md` | `2026-08-26.md` |
| `Meeting sept 8.md` | `2026-09-08.md` |
| `notes_2026-09-22.md` | `2026-09-22.md` |
| `oct6 meeting notes.md` | `2026-10-06.md` |
| `2026.10.20 minutes.md` | `2026-10-20.md` |
| `Nov 3 (final).md` | `2026-11-03.md` |

The 25 August file is `2026-08-26.md` because those minutes say the meeting was moved to 26 August after the storm. The index notes that. The minute texts themselves are unchanged.
thought:
Reading the notes and README to understand the content and naming conventions.Planning to standardize file names and add an index to the notes folder.

Most files use inconsistent date formats. The August 25 note should be renamed to 2026-08-26 to match the actual meeting date. Only one file already follows the ISO format.

Deciding between `YYYY-MM-DD.md` and `minutes-YYYY-MM-DD.md` for the file names. The existing `notes_2026-09-22.md` is a useful reference. Only file names and an index will be changed; note contents will stay untouched.

Settled on `YYYY-MM-DD.md` for the naming scheme. The August 25 note will be renamed to 2026-08-26 to match the actual meeting date, with a note in the index about the move from the 25th. Considering whether to update the README to mention the new index.

The README will remain unchanged. Only the notes folder will be modified.

The index will list meetings in chronological order with links, dates, and one-line summaries.

The index will be named `index.md` inside the notes folder.No other references were found. Files will be renamed with git mv or mv.

Files will be renamed to YYYY-MM-DD.md. An index.md will list them chronologically. The August 25/26 note will be dated 2026-08-26 based on its heading. The README will remain unchanged.

The index will be a markdown table with dates, links to each file, and brief summaries. The August 26 entry will note it was held a day late after the storm. The file will stay short and useful.

Drafting one-line summaries for each meeting to populate the index. The 2026-08-11 note covers noticeboard repaint, shed lights, and second tap. The 2026-08-26 note adds seed swap. The 2026-09-08 note covers roof replacement, fees, gate latch, and water bill. The 2026-09-22 note covers roof quote, compost order, and handing the second tap to Dov. The 2026-10-06 note covers roofer booking, fee reminders, gate latch volunteer, and winter checklist.

The 2026-10-20 note covers gate latch replacement, compost delivery, roof completion, and a work day. The 2026-11-03 note covers the roof invoice, work day plans, second tap, and water bill, and marks the final meeting of the year. The index will be named index.md. The YYYY-MM-DD format was chosen because it sorts correctly, avoids spaces and punctuation, and includes the year.

The existing `notes_2026-09-22.md` already used ISO dates, so the new naming is consistent. The November 3 note will be flagged as the final meeting of 2026. Note bodies will not be rewritten; only file names and the index will be changed.

The README will be updated with a one-line note pointing to the index, since it currently only describes the notes folder without indicating its purpose.

The README will remain untouched. The index will be a simple markdown table with dates, links, and brief subject lines. No open items or extra formatting will be added.File renames are complete. Now writing the index.The notes folder has been tidied. File names are now consistent. An index has been added.
